instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched ZBrush graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or any shell; do not run ZScript files, Python, macros, or other helper scripts/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only ZBrush native GUI tools, menus, brushes, and built-in export commands. Split a Multi-Polygroup Mesh into Named SubTools The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named MergedParts, is a single manifold mesh with exactly six polygroups. The polygroups partition all faces of the mesh into six non-overlapping regions. The mesh has no UVs, no polypaint, and no subdivision levels. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, split the SubTool into six independent SubTools, one per polygroup, rename them sequentially, and export the result as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Contains exactly six SubTools; their names are exactly the set {Part_01, Part_02, Part_03, Part_04, Part_05, Part_06}. No other SubTools are present, and no SubTool named MergedParts remains. - Each of the six SubTools carries exactly one polygroup. - The sum of face counts across the six SubTools equals the face count of the input MergedParts exactly. - The sum of vertex counts across the six SubTools is at most 1.5 x the input vertex count. - Each SubTool's faces form a single connected mesh.
